name: Runway
tagline: Generative video and creative AI tools for images, video, and editing

pricing.notes: Official pricing checked 2026-07-30; Standard plan listed at $15/month monthly and $12/month annually in public pricing references.

tiers.name: Standard
tiers.limits: 625 credits/month, shown as about 52 seconds of Gen-4.5; watermark removal and 4K upscale.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: 2,250 credits/month, shown as about 187 seconds of Gen-4.5; 500 GB storage.

tiers.name: Max
tiers.limits: 9,500 credits/month, shown as about 791 seconds of Gen-4.5; unused included credits can roll over for 1 month.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Custom credits, seats, security and support; public price is not listed.

pricing.freeTierCaps: 125 credits once, not monthly, plus 5 GB storage.
pricing.hiddenCosts: Standard and Pro included credits do not roll over; Max rolls them for only one month. Extra credit purchases start at 1,000 credits and do not expire.

verdictSummary: A UI around video models is buildable; the video-generation model quality, compute, safety, editing stack, and continuous research are not a solo afternoon project.
coreLoopDIY: Wrap open-source/video APIs to generate or edit clips, manage credits, and export assets.
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay because generative video quality and inference infrastructure are the product.

priorArt.name: diffusers
priorArt.desc: Open-source library for diffusion models; useful for experimentation, not a Runway replace

alternatives.name: ComfyUI
alternatives.desc: Images, video, masking, upscaling and effects in one graph; it replaces tools, not Runway's polish.

facts.install: Windows or macOS desktop installer, Windows portable archive, or manual Python install on Windows, macOS, or Linux
facts.engines: Local and downloadable image, video, audio, 3D, and text models including Stable Diffusion/SDXL/SD3.5, FLUX, Wan, LTX-Video, HunyuanVideo, CogVideoX, and Mochi; optional API nodes connect to hosted providers
facts.dataFormat: Models, inputs, outputs, and workflow JSON live in the local ComfyUI data tree; generated media can embed workflow and seed metadata, while API nodes transmit selected inputs to their provider
facts.gapVsPaid: It replaces many individual generation and masking operations, but not Runway's polished all-in-one editor, proprietary models, collaboration, or managed render farm.
facts.setupBlocker: A compatible GPU, enough VRAM and disk for multi-gigabyte models, and a working model/workflow must be chosen before useful output appears

alternatives.name: Draw Things
alternatives.desc: Local image and video generation on Apple hardware; a creator suite only if your editor lives elsewhere.

facts.install: Install the signed app from Apple's App Store on macOS, iPhone, or iPad
facts.engines: Runs supported Stable Diffusion, SDXL, FLUX, and video models locally, including imported checkpoints and LoRAs; optional cloud compute can offload generation
facts.dataFormat: Projects, models, history, and generated media live in the app sandbox; on macOS model files are under the app container, while cloud offload sends prompts and media for processing
facts.gapVsPaid: It handles generation and some edits locally, but remains an Apple-only generator rather than Runway's cross-platform collaborative creative suite.
facts.setupBlocker: Apple hardware is required, and the first model download is large; older devices can be slow or memory-limited

alternatives.name: LTX Desktop
alternatives.desc: The closest free thing to a generative video suite: local models, retakes and an actual editing timeline.

facts.install: Download the Windows .exe or macOS .dmg from the project's GitHub Releases page
facts.engines: LTX video models and bundled image-generation components, with optional LTX API and other configured hosted services; local generation is primarily supported on NVIDIA Windows systems
facts.dataFormat: Projects, settings, logs, downloaded models, source assets, and renders live in the platform-specific LTXDesktop application-data folder; API mode uploads the material needed for the requested generation
facts.gapVsPaid: It is the closest integrated editor here, yet still lacks Runway's proprietary models, mature browser collaboration, and cloud-scale inference.
facts.setupBlocker: Serious local generation currently needs a high-end NVIDIA Windows GPU and very large model downloads; macOS generation relies on an API key instead of local inference

alternatives.name: NodeTool
alternatives.desc: The rare open app with model workflows, masking and a video timeline; no included cloud render farm.

facts.install: Install the macOS .dmg, signed Windows .exe, or Linux AppImage; Docker Compose is available for self-hosting
facts.engines: Local Ollama, llama.cpp/GGUF, MLX, Nunchaku, Hugging Face, and diffusion/media models, plus BYOK providers such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, FAL, Replicate, KIE, ElevenLabs, and Hugging Face
facts.dataFormat: Workflows, projects, assets, files, provider settings, and vector indexes live locally in YAML, SQLite/SQLite-vec, and application storage; optional S3 or Supabase storage is supported, and cloud nodes transmit their inputs
facts.gapVsPaid: It combines model workflows, masking, and a timeline, but requires BYOK or local setup and lacks Runway's polished team and editor ecosystem.
facts.setupBlocker: No useful model or provider is bundled: the user must add an API key or download a multi-gigabyte local model, and some local backends add a large Python/Conda environment

alternatives.name: SwarmUI
alternatives.desc: A friendlier shell around local image and video workflows; editing remains thinner than Runway's.

facts.install: Run the Windows installer script, the Linux launch script, or install .NET/Python/Homebrew prerequisites and run launch-macos.sh on macOS; Docker is optional
facts.engines: Uses ComfyUI as its main backend for Stable Diffusion, SDXL, FLUX, Wan, LTX, MiniMax, ACE-Step, and other image/video/audio workflows; an Automatic1111-compatible backend is optional
facts.dataFormat: Configuration, users, models, workflows, generated media, and history live in the local SwarmUI installation and configured model/output directories
facts.gapVsPaid: It is a generation front end with deep workflows, not a full replacement for Runway's timeline editing, asset management, collaboration, and proprietary models.
facts.setupBlocker: The backend and models still have to be downloaded, and non-Windows installs require command-line prerequisites such as .NET, Python, and Git

alternatives.name: WanGP
alternatives.desc: A broad local image-and-video workbench; generation is free, the proprietary Runway models are not included.

facts.install: Run the supplied Windows install.bat or Linux/macOS install.sh script; community launchers such as Pinokio are optional
facts.engines: Local video, image, music, speech, and restoration models including Wan, MiniMax/Hailuo-family weights where available, LTX, Hunyuan, LongCat, Qwen Image, Z-Image, FLUX, ACE-Step, and Qwen TTS
facts.dataFormat: Downloaded models, presets, queues, galleries, generated media, and metadata live in the local installation tree and chosen output folders
facts.gapVsPaid: It covers more local models than Runway exposes, but lacks Runway's cohesive editing suite and team-oriented cloud workflow.
facts.setupBlocker: Installation must match the GPU and PyTorch/CUDA/ROCm stack, and useful models consume many gigabytes of disk and substantial VRAM

notes: Important no for the frontier-model category.
prompt:
Build me a thin video-generation workbench over hosted models, in place of
Runway. Requirements:

- A local web page on localhost:3300: Node + Express, a prompt box, a model
  picker, and a gallery of past generations.
- Generate via the Replicate API (token in .env) against current open video
  models (Wan/LTX/Hunyuan class). Pick one provider and stick to it; fal.ai
  only if it has a model Replicate lacks.
- Poll the job, download the mp4 to ~/generations/YYYY-MM-DD/, and record
  prompt, model, params, cost, and file path in SQLite (better-sqlite3).
- Image-to-video: upload a still and pass it as the conditioning frame.
- Show a month-to-date spend total computed from per-job cost so usage stays
  honest.
- No accounts, no telemetry; prompts and outputs stay local except the API
  calls themselves.
- Out of scope: editing timelines, inpainting, and anything realtime. Do not
  build model hosting or a job queue beyond simple polling.
- README: where to get the Replicate token, rough dollars per second of video
  on the default model, and a note that this rents models rather than replacing
  Runway, whose frontier video models and compute cannot be rebuilt solo.
